Description: ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby takes the inline stride apart into three components, each with its own drill: a powerful push out to the side, a glide on a centre or outside edge, and a set-down that does not land in a V. A session on the stride is a session on one move, and the drills are simply its three parts, taken one at a time and then put back together. Illustration generated with AI.

Title: Before Inline Skating: Rehearse Where Your Weight Goes, in Shoes
Description: A weight check to do at home in shoes, before the inline skates go on. ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby uses a simple standing exercise to show how the bend of the knees decides where the weight sits across the feet: knees straight and it drifts back; knees forward over the toes, body up, and it settles where it should. Skate day starts with that check, off the skates. Illustration generated with AI.

Description: ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby gives the hips their own off-skate work. Strengthening the muscles around the hips, all of the glutes above all, leaves an inline skater feeling more supported, more balanced and more in control on the wheels, and the hips are closely tied to how the lower back feels after a skate. This is preparation between sessions, not a fix during one. Illustration generated with AI.

Title: Off-Skate Training for Inline Skaters: One Leg, Locked Knee, a Minute Each Side
Description: An off-skates one-leg exercise: bent-knee inline skating rarely works the thigh fully straight. ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby balances that off the skates: stand on one leg, lift the other to right angles, tense and lock the standing leg, hold a minute, twice each side. The standing leg is the one being trained. If balance goes, the free foot stays near the floor, or on it. Illustration generated with AI.

Description: ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby has never lifted a weight in a gym: lifting your own body is enough, and most skaters find out how hard that is on the first back exercise. Mobility for the feet and ankles therefore lives off the skates, and ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby places it at the end: her foot and ankle movements work best done after the session, once the boots come off. Title: Three Floor Stretches Close an Inline Session
Description: ICP-certified coach Asha Kirkby ends an inline skate with three stretches on the floor, in this order. Seated forward fold: legs out, a gentle lean over the thighs, kept light, or hug the knees. Half reclining side press: from the same L-sit, a small half press-up each side. Reclined twist: on your back, knees dropped to one side, head to the other, a few breaths, then switch. Illustration generated with AI.
